subject: Data Export / DPF evidence request + DPA annex clarifications (CardinalRx RFP)
messages:
From: Marco DeLucca <marco@cardinalrx.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: CardinalRx Procurement <procurement@cardinalrx.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: RFP: data export / DPF evidence needed for EU-US flows

Hi Grace / Ben,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week. CardinalRx is progressing this RFP to final legal/tech review. Procurement has asked for a compact DPF (data protection framework) evidence pack and a draft DPA annex that clarifies cross-border safeguards for EU personal data going to the US.

To keep the review tight, can you provide the following by EOD next Thursday:
- A concise export-controls matrix showing: which data types may be routed outside the EU, available routing/residency controls, and fallback behaviors.
- Technical evidence for cross-border processing: key management residency options (KMS/HSM), ability to pin keys to EU KMS, and whether model-inference KV cache ever persists outside EU region.
- A copy of your current DPA annex with any redlines that affect subprocessor clauses and transfer mechanisms (SCCs/DPF references).
- Logging/retention specifics for access logs and audit trails (schema + retention periods).

Procurement attached a short questionnaire (attached). Please confirm if Redwood can deliver a one-week turnaround.

Appreciate it — if a quick sync is easier, we can do a 30-min call tomorrow afternoon.

Best,
Marco
Head of Procurement, CardinalRx

Attachment: cardinalrx_dpf_questions.pdf
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marco DeLucca <marco@cardinalrx.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 12:08:00 +0000
Subject: Re: RFP: data export / DPF evidence needed for EU-US flows

Marco — thanks for the clear list. We can meet the one-week goal; attached are the initial artifacts that match your asks. High-level answers below and details in attachments.

Attachments sent: export-controls-matrix.xlsx, dpa-annex-redline.pdf (legal redline), export-controls-evidence.zip (operational snapshots).

Quick summary:
- Residency controls: hosted Redwood API supports region pinning per-customer (EU only) for both inference and cache. For Hosted customers we offer EU-region-only routing; Dedicated/Private can be deployed into customer VPC in EU.
- KMS options: we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS/CloudHSM and BYOK flows. Keys can be constrained to EU regions; we also support HSM-backed import for Dedicated/Private.
- KV cache behavior: KV cache used for streaming inference is ephemeral and cleared on session end by default. For customers requesting strict residency we offer no-cross-region cache eviction policies and can isolate cache to EU nodes.
- Transfer legal basis / DPA: we rely on SCCs for standard hosted flows and provide a DPF supplement for customers requiring transfer impacts. Laura has included redlines to the DPA annex — see dpa-annex-redline.pdf.
- Logging/retention: Audit logs (request metadata, routing decisions) retained 1 year by default; we can extend to 3 years on enterprise plans. Schema sample in the matrix.

Next steps:
1) Laura to confirm any DPA language changes (she's on copy).
2) David to provide a short attestation note on KV caching and KMS controls.
3) Ben will coordinate exec approvals and finalize commercial terms.

If helpful, Ben and I can take the procurement questionnaire now and propose a one-week delivery schedule for the remaining evidence.

— Grace
VP, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: export-controls-matrix.xlsx, dpa-annex-redline.pdf, export-controls-evidence.zip
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marco DeLucca <marco@cardinalrx.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 08:47:00 +0000
Subject: Re: RFP: data export / DPF evidence needed for EU-US flows

Marco—

Thanks for the request. I've reviewed the DPA annex and proposed targeted language to address two procurement priorities:

1) Transfer mechanism: we accept SCCs and provide a DPF supplement outlining technical and organizational measures. Proposed clause: "Provider will implement region-pinning and KMS isolation measures as described in Annex X; where Customer requests EU-only processing, Provider will route both inference and transient KV cache exclusively to EU nodes."

2) Subprocessor transparency: we propose a 30-day notice window before onboarding new subprocessors with a right for Customer to object on reasonable grounds tied to data residency or regulatory constraints.

I've attached the redline (dpa-annex-redline.pdf). Two asks for you to confirm:
- Does CardinalRx require HSM-backed BYOK for initial go-live? If yes, we need to add an operational SOW.
- Any required retention longer than 1 year for audit logs — if so, specify target retention and whether logs must remain in-region.

If you prefer, we can prepare a DocuSign-ready version once the wording is accepted.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
From: Marco DeLucca <marco@cardinalrx.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: CardinalRx Procurement <procurement@cardinalrx.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: RFP: data export / DPF evidence needed for EU-US flows

Thanks Grace/Laura — received the matrix and redline. A couple clarifications from procurement:
- CardinalRx prefers HSM-backed BYOK for the pilot; please confirm whether that is supported for Dedicated or Hosted with customer-managed HSM.
- Procurement would like an explicit statement that audit logs containing personal data markers will remain in-region for EU customers.

We can accept the redline language in principle; procurement will need the DocuSign-ready annex and a short operational SOW for KMS work.

Also attaching our procurement checklist (procurement-requirements.docx). Can your team confirm a go-live/PO acceptance checklist and an estimated delivery timeline (we're targeting an internal approval meeting on 19 Nov).

On cadence — a 30-min call tomorrow (11 Nov at 14:00 CET) would be helpful.

Best,
Marco
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marco DeLucca <marco@cardinalrx.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 14:35:00 +0000
Subject: Re: RFP: data export / DPF evidence needed for EU-US flows

Marco — great to get this moving.

Short answers:
- HSM-backed BYOK: supported for Dedicated and Private deployments; for Hosted we support customer-managed KMS keys constrained to EU regions and can arrange HSM-backed imports in most cloud providers — David will confirm specifics.
- Audit logs: we can provide an in-region retention option for audit logs on enterprise plans; we will include the retention configuration in the SOW.

Action plan:
1) David will provide a one-page attestation on KMS and KV cache residency by EOD Friday.
2) Laura will prepare the DocuSign-ready DPA annex (target: 12 Nov EOD).
3) Grace / I will produce the PO/go-live checklist and estimated delivery windows (target: 13 Nov morning).

I'll schedule the 30-min call for tomorrow 14:00 CET and send a calendar invite (link below). If the CardinalRx procurement team wants to push the internal approval earlier, we'll accelerate.

Calendar invite: https://cal.redwoodinference.com/meet/ben/30/11nov14

Thanks — Ben
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
